thread:
mina.kim: Heads-up — atlas-3b int8 bring-up on the vertical-KR OCR dataset is showing a consistent BLEU drop vs fp16 baseline (dev split).

samir.ahmed: Numbers?

eval-bot: quick summary: atlas-3b_fp16 baseline: BLEU=28.4, ppl=12.1
atlas-3b_int8 (same tokenizer): BLEU=23.7, ppl=18.9
(averaged over 3 runs, beam=5)

hana.choi: who did the tokenization asserts? could be a detok / normalization mismatch for vertical text.

mina.kim: I ran a diff on token counts — many Hangul syllables are split into Jamo tokens after quantized tokenizer path:
```
# repro snippet
from hf_tokenizers import AtlasTokenizer
tok = AtlasTokenizer.from_pretrained('redwood/atlas-tokenizer')
print(tok.encode('각').tokens)
# -> ['ᄀ', 'ᅡ', 'ᆨ']  # decomposed Jamo
```

jay.ortiz: That matches my local run. The fp16 path uses upstream HF tokenizer with NFKC composition step; the int8 runtime feed seems to be using normalized NFD-like input (decomposed). Probably a normalization/byte mapping bug in the quantized model's preprocessing.

samir.ahmed: Is this specific to vertical text? Why dataset matters: vertical OCR output tends to include VS-1/2, line-sep chars, and thin spaces. Those chars can trigger different grapheme normalization.

mina.kim: Repro steps I used:
```
gsutil cp -r gs://redwood-evals/vertical-kr/dev/* .
python eval.py --model atlas-3b-int8 --tokenizer redwood/atlas-tokenizer --detok-mode legacy --beam 5
```

hana.choi: Can you attach a minimal failing example (1-2 sentences) so we can bisect tokenizer vs runtime?

mina.kim: Pasted one:
Input (OCR vertical): "단\n영"  (two-line vertical that should compose to "다영")
fp16 output tokens: ["다영"]
int8 output tokens: ["ᄃ", "ᅡ", "ᆫ", "\n", "ᄋ", "ᅧ", "ᆼ"]  -> breaks translation model context, BLEU drops

samir.ahmed: If the tokenizer is decomposing, model's embedding table may not have composed syllables -> different token ids entirely. That will wreck BLEU.

jay.ortiz: Quick mitigation: in the eval harness insert explicit Unicode NFC/NFKC composition before tokenization. Try `unicodedata.normalize('NFC', s)` at preprocessing to see if BLEU recovers.

mina.kim: I ran NFC pass — BLEU moves back up to ~27.8 (not fully fp16 but close). So normalization explains most of it.

hana.choi: OK good. We need a long-term fix: either ensure quantized runtime applies same normalization, or make tokenizer robust to vertical/VS controls.

samir.ahmed: Action items: 1) eng-ml to add NFC step to the int8 preprocessing by default for KR vertical pipeline. 2) infra to schedule a re-quantize build that preserves HF tokenizer codepath (avoid custom fast-path that strips normalization). 3) QA to add vertical-KR tests to regression suite.

jay.ortiz: I'll open a PR with the NFC change in the eval harness and a small test. tagging @eng-infra for re-quantize.

mina.kim: FYI logs + sample inputs uploaded to gs://redwood-evals/vertical-kr/int8-jamo-debug/ (see manifest.txt).

eval-bot: regression alert created: r/atlas-3b-int8/2026-03-19-bleu-drop. Linked QA ticket #4672.

hana.choi: Can we canary the patched int8 in asia-east1 only? avoid global rollout until re-quant check.

samir.ahmed: +1. Also add fallback policy: if tokenizer mismatch detected (high jamo token rate), route requests to fp16/dedicated backend.

mina.kim: Thanks — I'll follow up with a short write-up and a minimal test to add to the nightly evals. :thumbsup:

jay.ortiz: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/atlas-evals/pull/182 (NFC pre-tokenize + test). Please review.

hana.choi: Reviewed, left minor comments.

mina.kim: TL;DR: root cause = unicode normalization + vertical OCR control chars exposing a preprocessing divergence in the int8 serving path. NFC pre-tokenize is a safe immediate mitigation. Longer-term: unify preprocessing between quant/runtime and hf tokenizer.

samir.ahmed: Nice catch. Good regression write-up, Mina.
